display.title: Episode 422: The Mystery of Dayeinu (Rosh Chodesh Nissan)
display.summary_short: Rosh Chodesh Nissan, the month of miracles; saying the Shema at bedtime to begin the day the night before; and the Pesach story of Reb Sholom and Dayeinu.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Rosh Chodesh Nissan 5750. Uncle Yossi explains that Nissan is a month of miracles, and shares the Rebbe's teaching that the letters of the year 5750 stand for 'a year of miracles', with a prayer that the final redemption come in Nissan. The Hakochainik march is sung to the tune of Mi Mitzrayim Ge'altanu. Mitzvah Time teaches that a Jewish day begins the night before, as the Torah says 'it was evening and it was morning', so the Shema at bedtime starts our day; Hashem protects us through the night and gives us pleasant sleep. Children who cannot read Hebrew may say it in any language, and a transliterated Shema sheet is offered by mail. A seventh-grade girl answers a phone quiz on stretching the word Echad and leads the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time tells of Reb Sholom, a poor man famous for hachnasas orchim, who prayed for help before Pesach; through the king's lost ring and the song Dayeinu at his Seder, Hashem sent him a great reward. The show ends with an invitation to a Tzivos Hashem Chol HaMoed event.
display.lesson: Begin each day with the Shema the night before, and trust that Hashem helps those who devote themselves to hachnasas orchim.

date.note: 'Today is Rosh Chodesh Nissan'; 1 Nissan 5750 was Tuesday 27 March 1990, matching the weekly estimate.
